Run-time modifiers for generated materials

Textures and materials are generated, so the baked PNG is not the only product: the same material can react to the world without re-baking its maps. A modifier is a few numbers the shader applies on top of the material, so a script can wet a rock when it rains, cover a roof with snow or age a wall.

Modifier Range Effect
Tint colour, white = none multiplies the albedo (season shift, team colour)
Wetness 0 dry .. 1 soaked darker albedo and a glossy film (low roughness)
Snow 0 none .. 1 everything facing up white, rough cover on upward faces; the more snow, the further down the slopes it reaches
Age 0 new .. 1 old washed-out, darker, rougher

Where they live#

  • In the material (.mat keys mod_tint, mod_wetness, mod_snow, mod_age; MaterialSurface, C ABI v10, the Material panel's Run-time modifiers section): the defaults a material ships with.
  • On the entity (Mesh Renderer fields Tint, Wetness, Snow, Age, saved with the scene): the values a game changes at run time. They are ordinary reflected fields, so scripts read and write them like any other (Mesh Renderer, Wetness, 0..1), and so do the Inspector and the agent bridge.
  • The renderer combines both: tints multiply, the amounts add and clamp to 0..1. Entities that share one material and one mesh still batch only when their modifiers are equal.

Scenes saved before the fields existed load with neutral modifiers.

What is not here yet#

  • Modifiers that need new maps (damage decals, moss growing in cracks) still need the generator's graph at run time; the graph and its parameter schema are not shipped with the baked output yet.
  • Foliage wind and translucency (wind_*, translucency) are material-only, not per entity.
